conf.description: cribl-internal audit via version-control REST API: two discriminated response shapes (commit call vs deploy call) branched on presence of 'commit', event.action set per-branch from which endpoint was called, version/configVersion collapsed onto one cribl.config.version per the work order's own instruction not to emit both keys.

conf.comment: cribl-internal/audit/api-pull. REST Collector against POST /api/v1/version/commit and PATCH .../deploy -- two discriminated response shapes landing in one pipeline, branched on presence of 'commit' (commit response) vs its absence (deploy response), mirroring this technology's internal-metrics discriminated-union precedent. event.action is a per-branch constant ('commit'/'deploy') reflecting which endpoint was called, not a guessed field. version/configVersion collapse onto one cribl.config.version per the work order's instruction ('do not emit both keys'). Per recommendations.direct.cribl: neither response shape carries an actor or a commit timestamp (git metadata only), so this feed is NOT a substitute for audit.log collection -- a coverage note, not something a pipeline can fix. Only file paths are pulled (files.modified/files.created), never file contents, so no masking was needed for those.

functions.description: document the two-branch discriminated-union shape and the actor/timestamp coverage gap
commit-response branch: git diff summary and changed-file paths (never contents), commit hash echoed to cribl.config.version

deploy-response branch (complement of the commit branch): target Worker Group, deployed config version sourced from whichever of configVersion/version is present per the work order's do-not-emit-both instruction, tags left untouched since its vendor name already matches its ECS target

dataset/category tags (unconditional, shared by both branches), cleanup of every now-consumed original key from both response shapes; 'message' and 'tags' are untouched since their vendor names already match their ECS targets
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
